## Cultural journeys through Belize, Guatemala and Costa Rica

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [26-day itinerary through eight Central American countries](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) includes Belize, Guatemala and Costa Rica alongside Mexico, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Panama. Belize and Guatemala are visited consecutively, but several other countries come before Costa Rica. This is **a thematic intersection within an extended tour**, not a separate direct journey limited to these three countries.

The historical story begins at [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/) and continues at [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). Ancient ruins then give way to colonial streets and living community traditions. In Costa Rica, the itinerary shifts its emphasis to nature. No dedicated archaeological or museum excursion in Costa Rica is scheduled.

| Country | Main part of the itinerary |
|---|---|
| Belize | The Maya city of Caracol |
| Guatemala | Tikal, Antigua, Atitlán |
| Costa Rica | Forests, volcano and canals |

## Belize: Maya history at Caracol

After the Mexican section, a flight from Cancún to Belize City and a transfer to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/) are planned. From there, travellers take a full-day [excursion to Caracol, Rio Frio and Rio On](/belize/caracol/caracol-rio-frio-rio-on-pools/).

At the archaeological site of [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/), visitors discover ancient Maya architecture, including an ascent of Caana. This is the main historical stop in Belize. The second part of the day takes place in [Mountain Pine Ridge](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/), with visits to [Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) and the [Rio On Pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/), where swimming and relaxation are planned.

Archaeology and nature therefore share the same day. Exploring a temple and relaxing beside water, however, involve different amounts of time and physical effort. If detailed explanations of Maya culture and a longer visit to the ruins matter to you, discuss the pace when arranging the itinerary. Other options can be found among [cultural tours through Belize](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/belize/).

## Guatemala: Tikal and crafts around Lake Atitlán

After San Ignacio, the route crosses the land border and proceeds to [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). The [guided archaeological tour of Tikal](/guatemala/tikal-and-flores/tikal-archaeology-guided-visit/) explores the temples and monuments of the ancient Maya city amid tropical forest. UNESCO recognises Tikal as a major archaeological landscape where historical heritage is intertwined with protected natural areas. The group spends the night in the Flores area.

Next comes a flight to Guatemala City, followed by [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/). The itinerary includes a walk through the historic centre and an introduction to textile traditions in San Antonio Aguas Calientes and Santiago Zamora. Here history continues in workshops and daily life rather than being confined to stone ruins.

At [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), the group visits [San Juan La Laguna](/guatemala/place/san-juan-la-laguna/), known for its galleries, textile cooperatives and traditional medicinal herbs. A boat then takes travellers to Santiago Atitlán. On this [excursion to Atitlán's communities](/guatemala/lake-atitlan/atitlan-san-juan-textiles-santiago-culture/), the cultural experience centres on living local traditions. Longer encounters with this heritage can be compared in the [Guatemala culture and history catalogue](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/guatemala/).

A separate [hike up Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/pacaya-volcano/pacaya-volcano-hike-1900-2300/) is scheduled, covering elevations of approximately 1,900–2,300 metres. This day appeals to nature lovers and hikers, but it is not itself a historical excursion.

## Costa Rica: the nature section of a longer journey

Costa Rica is reached after Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua. Travellers fly from Managua to San José, then continue to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). A [cloud forest walk](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-cloud-forest-reserve-walk/) and a canopy tour are scheduled. Later come the El Tigre waterfalls hike, the [Arenal area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), hanging bridges and a trail across old lava flows.

Costa Rica's section concludes with the [Tortuguero canals](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) and a [boat excursion at dawn](/costa-rica/tortuguero/tortuguero-dawn-canals-boat/). This is an independent nature experience, distinct from Caracol, Tikal and the textile workshops of Atitlán. **The tour does not include mandatory museum or archaeological visits in Costa Rica.** Understanding that distinction helps travellers plan for the experiences genuinely offered and decide whether additional cultural stops are desirable.

## How to divide your time between history and nature

The route changes both the kind of excursions and the transport used: a flight to Belize from Mexico, an overland crossing into Guatemala, a domestic flight before Antigua, further Central American countries and a flight from Managua to San José. The Guatemala–Costa Rica leg is **not a direct transfer**.

At Caracol and Tikal, the amount of daylight and site access matter; in Antigua and Atitlán, workshop schedules and time for unhurried walks are more important. Costa Rica adds humid forests, active walking and water transport. Comfortable footwear, rain protection and sensible pacing will be more useful than trying to follow the same relaxed city-walking routine everywhere.

Border documentation and entry conditions depend on nationality and each country's current rules. We can help coordinate sightseeing days with flights and road transfers and discuss where additional time for cultural experiences is needed.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days}}

## Frequently asked questions about the culture of Belize, Guatemala and Costa Rica

### Can Caracol and Tikal be visited on the same trip?

Yes. The current [26-day tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) includes [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/) in Belize and [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) in Guatemala, with an overland border crossing between them.

### Does the tour introduce Guatemala's craft traditions?

Yes. The itinerary includes textile traditions near Antigua and visits to cooperatives in [San Juan La Laguna](/guatemala/place/san-juan-la-laguna/). Particular meetings and their timing depend on the excursion programme.

### Are historical museums included in Costa Rica?

The tour does not list a dedicated museum day in Costa Rica. Its principal stops there focus on cloud forests, Arenal and Tortuguero.

### Are the three countries visited one after another?

No. Belize and Guatemala come consecutively, but Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua are also visited before Costa Rica.

## Nature in Belize, Guatemala and Costa Rica on one journey

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. We offer the [“Central America: Eight Countries in 26 Days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/). It starts in Mexico and continues through Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. **The three countries named in the catalogue do not limit the entire trip to those destinations.**

The principal nature-focused reason to choose this combination is the transition from Belize's forests and rivers to Guatemala's volcanic highlands and Costa Rica's varied natural regions. Archaeological sites, cities and local traditions also occupy a substantial part of the programme. The journey suits travellers who enjoy combining culture and nature on an extended itinerary.

Compare options without a thematic filter in the [Belize + Costa Rica + Guatemala selection](/multi-country/belize_costa-rica_guatemala/). Other nature travel formats are presented in the ['Nature' section](/interests/nature/).

## Belize: forest roads, a cave and natural pools

On day six, travellers fly from Cancún to Belize City and transfer to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/). The following full day combines the archaeological site of [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/) with the natural attractions of [Mountain Pine Ridge](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/). The return route includes [Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) and the [Rio On natural pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/).

This sequence makes it possible to see a limestone cave and a river landscape on the same excursion. Swimming and time to relax are listed at the pools. Actual water access, road conditions and whether swimming is permitted depend on the weather and the decisions of the accompanying guides.

After the overnight stay in Belize, the route crosses into Guatemala the next day. Additional days on the islands, dedicated diving or safaris cannot simply be added without changing the programme. These activities exist in Belize but do not form separate sections of the tour described here.

## Guatemala: Tikal, Pacaya and Lake Atitlán

The Guatemalan section begins at [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), where Maya temples stand in the tropical forest of Petén. Travellers encounter both history and the natural setting of the monument. Yet a visit to the ruins must not be described as a specially organised wildlife-watching excursion.

Next come a flight to Guatemala City, a walk in [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/) and a trip to [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/). The hike ascends from approximately 1,900 to 2,300 metres above sea level. The main crater is higher, and reaching it is not included in the excursion. Suitable footwear, readiness for the ascent and current volcano access restrictions all matter.

The group then travels to [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/). Here the volcanic trail gives way to lakeside views, a boat crossing and visits to San Juan La Laguna and Santiago Atitlán. The programme also introduces local textile traditions. These are different experiences: the lake landscape and cultural stops complement one another.

Belize and Guatemala are linked by a consecutive border crossing on the actual route. The journey then continues through Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua before finally reaching Costa Rica.

## Costa Rica: from cloud forest to the Tortuguero canals

The Costa Rican leg begins on day eighteen with a flight from Managua to San José and a transfer to [Monteverde and Santa Elena](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). A cloud forest walk and canopy activity are scheduled next. They place different demands on participants: canopy activities require a separate briefing and compliance with safety rules.

The next stop is [El Tigre Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/el-tigre-waterfalls/). Its walking route takes about three hours, with moderate to strenuous sections and river crossings. The itinerary then continues to [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), hanging bridges and volcanic trails. Paths may be slippery in wet conditions, which should be considered when choosing footwear and pace.

The nature-focused section concludes in [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) with an early morning boat trip through the canals. Travellers may observe birds and other forest inhabitants, but sightings of specific species on any particular day cannot be guaranteed. The group then continues to Panama.

Costa Rica receives several consecutive nature days, compared with Belize's eventful but brief excursion. This difference is important when choosing the programme.

## How the stops and physical demands are distributed

| Country | Natural attractions |
|---|---|
| Belize | Mountain Pine Ridge, Rio Frio, Rio On |
| Guatemala | Tikal forest, Pacaya, Atitlán |
| Costa Rica | Monteverde, El Tigre, Arenal, Tortuguero |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days}}

**The 26 days cover the complete eight-country journey.** Adding up the durations of the named nature excursions does not turn them into a ready-made three-country tour. Limiting the route to Belize, Guatemala and Costa Rica would require a new agreement on the route, flights, nights and commercial terms.

The 26-day tour does not state a specific total price. To calculate the trip, Ada Tours clarifies the flights, hotel categories, accommodation arrangements and individual terms. An invented minimum price or a price for only three of the countries cannot be quoted here.

## Weather, borders and payments: practical preparation

One journey combines forest roads and rivers in Belize, a high-altitude ascent in Guatemala and humid trails in Costa Rica. Pacaya calls for comfortable shoes and additional clothing layers; Monteverde requires rain protection; a waterproof cover is useful for equipment on the Tortuguero boat. Consider your physical capacity for the El Tigre hike before departure.

Different currencies are used: the Belize dollar, Guatemalan quetzal and Costa Rican colón. The official reference buying rate of the Central Bank of Belize is 2 BZD per 1 USD, but bank fees and the cost of individual transactions differ. Whether US dollars or a particular Russian or foreign bank card can be used needs to be checked at each stop; there is no single dependable payment method for all three countries.

Visa requirements depend on nationality and on travelling **through all eight countries**. A land crossing between Belize and Guatemala requires valid documents and compliance with the rules of both sides. Costa Rica's official portal specifies a requirement for proof of onward departure. Ada Tours can help organise the sequence of transfers and identify the documents and deadlines to check before booking.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Belize, Guatemala and Costa Rica

### Is this a ready-made tour limited to three countries?

No. This selection contains a 26-day programme across eight countries. A three-country version would require new planning and logistics.

### Which nature days involve the most activity?

In Guatemala, the ascent of Pacaya; in Costa Rica, the El Tigre hike and canopy experience. Regular forest walks and boat excursions involve different levels of effort.

### Are wildlife sightings in Tortuguero guaranteed?

No. A boat trip through the canals is included, but the species and number of encounters depend on the season and natural conditions.

### Does the Belize section include a beach stay or diving?

On this programme, Belize covers San Ignacio, Caracol, the cave and the pools. There is no dedicated diving section.

### Which documents should be checked?

Entry and transit rules for every country according to nationality, passport validity, any applicable re-entry conditions and proof of onward travel.

## Wildlife and safari: encounters on a route through Belize, Costa Rica and Guatemala

Belize, Costa Rica and Guatemala offer access to very different natural environments. Our [“Central America: Eight Countries in 26 Days” programme](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), however, **is not a standalone tour of these three countries only**. The itinerary also passes through Mexico, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Panama.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The 'Wildlife and Safari' classification comes from included walks in Monteverde's cloud forest and dawn wildlife watching on the Tortuguero canals in Costa Rica. Belize's forests and Guatemala's Tikal add landscapes and archaeology to the extended tour, but do not imply an included safari in each country. Compare the actual visiting arrangements and time allocated to each area, rather than an assumed number of animal encounters.

## Belize: pine reserve, rivers and Rio Frio Cave

Travellers fly to Belize from Cancún and then transfer to San Ignacio. The next day visits [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/) and [Mountain Pine Ridge Forest Reserve](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/). The itinerary includes an ancient Maya complex, Rio Frio Cave and the Rio On Pools.

The nature section consists of **forest landscapes, river, cave and stops beside the water**. It contrasts with the humid tropical forests of Guatemala and Costa Rica. But Belize's scheduled day does not include a dedicated early morning ornithology excursion, a night safari or a list of animals the guide is guaranteed to show.

Caracol is primarily an archaeological destination. Exploring the ancient complex takes place in a forested environment, but is not the same as professional birdwatching. If particular Belizean animals are the main purpose of your journey, a separate nature programme will be required.

## Guatemala: Tikal's forest setting around Maya heritage

The route crosses from Belize into Guatemala towards [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). A visit to the Maya temple complex amid tropical forest is included. Tikal matters both as an archaeological site and as a protected natural environment, with forest surrounding the ancient plazas and pyramids.

On the trails, you may hear birds or see insects and other forest inhabitants, but **the excursion primarily explores archaeology**. Encounters with jaguars, monkeys or any particular bird species cannot be promised at a specific time. Sightings depend on visitor conditions, animal behaviour and the authorised routes.

Subsequent days in Guatemala focus on Antigua, Pacaya Volcano and Lake Atitlán. These are compelling landscapes and cultural stops, but on the itinerary in question they do not replace a specialised wildlife-watching programme. This distinction helps set realistic expectations: Guatemala's natural environments are part of the journey, though dedicated ecological excursions take less time here than in Costa Rica.

## Costa Rica: cloud forest, Arenal and canals at dawn

The most substantial wildlife-oriented part of the tour is in Costa Rica. After flying from Managua, the group travels to [Monteverde and Santa Elena](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). A cloud forest walk is scheduled the following morning, with a canopy activity in the afternoon. The tour mentions a possible quetzal sighting but explicitly says that an encounter with the bird is **not guaranteed**.

After Monteverde come El Tigre Waterfalls and the Arenal area, with hanging bridges and a walk through a volcanic park. This gives travellers several ways to experience the forest: on foot along trails and from above on bridges. Animals may appear, but the excursion route and the likelihood of a sighting are different matters.

Travellers then proceed to [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). Here the programme includes **a dawn boat excursion along the national park's canals** to observe its inhabitants. Together with Monteverde's cloud forest, this day is particularly important for the 'Wildlife and Safari' theme.

Tortuguero is a humid lowland area on the Caribbean coast with a network of rivers and canals. Conditions differ from the cooler, mountainous Monteverde: waterproof protection matters on the boat, and comfortable nonslip shoes on forest trails. The sea turtle nesting season must not automatically be treated as part of this tour: no separate night excursion to nesting beaches is listed.

## How Belize, Guatemala and Costa Rica are connected

The full itinerary follows this order: **Belize → Guatemala → Honduras → El Salvador → Nicaragua → Costa Rica**. There is no direct 'Tikal–Monteverde' transfer. Other countries, archaeological sites and cities lie between them, followed by a flight from Managua to San José.

For that reason, recovery time after travel matters as much as the list of natural attractions. Birdwatching in Monteverde and observing Tortuguero's wildlife work best if the scheduled nature days are not cut short to fit in another city. The progression of landscapes also illustrates the difference between Belize's forests and Costa Rica's humid canals.

When designing a private itinerary, we can discuss the number of nights and choice of natural areas. That would, however, be a new product, not simply a shortened version of the ready-made tour at its existing price.

## Preparing for walks and wildlife observation

Closed shoes and lightweight clothing for hot weather are useful for the trails and cave; an additional layer for cool, rainy conditions is wise in Monteverde. In Tortuguero, a waterproof document case and binoculars are practical if birds are a particular interest. The tour does not confirm that personal equipment is provided within the price.

The timing of wildlife outings matters: the canal excursion is deliberately scheduled at dawn. On other parts of the journey, the chance of encountering particular birds or animals cannot be inferred from a reserve's name alone. Park access, guiding regulations and opening times should be checked against official information before travelling.

Each of the three countries has its own entry rules. For a journey through eight countries, the entire route, flights and border crossings must be checked; requirements depend on nationality and apply on specific dates.

Compare other 'Wildlife and Safari' itineraries in the catalogues featuring [Belize](/interests/wildlife/tours/belize/), [Costa Rica](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/) and [Guatemala](/interests/wildlife/tours/guatemala/). On multicountry tours, wildlife watching may occur in another country along the route, so check the specific included days. The combination without a thematic filter can be found in the [three-country catalogue](/multi-country/belize_costa-rica_guatemala/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days}}

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife in Belize, Guatemala and Costa Rica

### Where are the most wildlife-watching opportunities on this itinerary?

In Costa Rica: a walk in Monteverde's cloud forest and a dawn boat trip through Tortuguero's canals are included. Belize focuses on Caracol, its pine reserve, cave and natural pools; Guatemala focuses on Tikal's jungle setting.

### Is seeing a quetzal in Monteverde guaranteed?

No. The [tour programme](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) mentions a possible quetzal sighting without guaranteeing it. Wildlife encounters always depend on local conditions.

### Is turtle nesting observation included in Tortuguero?

A morning boat excursion through the canals is confirmed. A separate visit to the nesting beaches during turtle season is not listed as an included activity.

### Can the three countries be visited consecutively without other stops?

The current 26-day route passes through eight countries; Honduras, El Salvador and Nicaragua lie between Guatemala and Costa Rica. A direct three-country option would need to be arranged separately.

## Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Costa Rica: what connects them on one journey?

**This combination suits travellers wishing to discover ancient Maya centres, highland cities and tropical forests on one trip.** Mainland [Belize](/belize/) provides a starting point for Caracol and the natural areas of Cayo. In [Guatemala](/guatemala/), the journey continues through Tikal, Antigua and Lake Atitlán. In [Honduras](/honduras/), Copán is the central stop, famous for its carved stelae and Hieroglyphic Stairway. [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) brings a change of focus, with cloud forests, Arenal Volcano, rivers and the Tortuguero canals coming to the fore.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. These are itineraries that include **all four countries among their main destinations**. The selection does not imply that the programme is limited to these nations.

The current [“Central America: Eight Countries in 26 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) also visits Mexico, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Panama. It proceeds from north to south, from Mexico City to Panama City. Look beyond the country names in the catalogue and consider the actual stops, flights and overnight stays.

## Places included in the current programme

| Country | Main stops |
|---|---|
| Belize | San Ignacio, Caracol, Rio Frio |
| Guatemala | Tikal, Antigua, Pacaya, Atitlán |
| Honduras | Copán and the archaeological complex |
| Costa Rica | Monteverde, Arenal, Tortuguero |

**Belize, days 6–7.** Following a flight from Cancún, the group lands in Belize City and transfers to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/). The next day is devoted to [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/); the itinerary also includes [Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) and the [Rio On natural pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/). This is the mainland part of Belize. No visit to Belize's reefs or islands is listed on this particular 26-day route, although other programmes in the country may offer them.

**Guatemala, days 8–11.** The route crosses the land border from Belize and continues to [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). A domestic flight within Guatemala, [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), an ascent of [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/) and visits to villages around [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/) follow. The transition from hot Petén to the highlands calls for different clothing and involves different physical demands.

**Honduras, days 12–13.** Travellers come from the Atitlán area to Copán and visit the [Copán ruins](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/). Time should be reserved for its stelae and Hieroglyphic Stairway: the site is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The group then continues to El Salvador. On this tour, Honduras is a short but substantial archaeological section, not an extended beach holiday.

**Costa Rica, days 18–23.** Following a flight from Managua to San José, the route takes travellers into [Monteverde's cloud forests](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), then to El Tigre Waterfalls and the [La Fortuna and Arenal area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). The final nature section follows the canals of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). Bird and animal sightings depend on natural conditions; a guaranteed list of species cannot be promised.

## Why the borders of the four selected countries are not the whole story

Belize and Guatemala share a land border, and the itinerary crosses it between San Ignacio and Tikal. The journey then continues from Guatemala to Honduras. **Honduras does not share a border with Costa Rica.** Nicaragua lies between them, and the actual 26-day itinerary also includes a stop in El Salvador.

The Honduras–Costa Rica section therefore cannot be described as a direct crossing between neighbouring countries. The existing tour has separate stages in El Salvador and Nicaragua, followed by a flight from Managua to San José. Travelling only to the named four countries would require a different transport plan, with separately confirmed flights and connections.

For multicountry travel, we can help compare days spent on the road, border crossings, arrival times for excursions and connection windows. Allow time for passport checks and baggage collection. On separately purchased tickets, a short connection could mean missing the next flight and part of the sightseeing programme.

## Entry documents: an example for Russian citizens

**The information below was checked against official sources on October 15, 2026, for Russian citizens holding ordinary international passports.** Rules may differ for other nationalities; they should be checked again for all countries and border crossings before buying tickets.

Belize's government grants Russian citizens a visa exemption for stays of up to **90 days**. This does not remove the need to check passport validity, the purpose of travel, return or onward tickets and the carrier's requirements.

Guatemala and Honduras participate in the **CA-4** agreement alongside El Salvador and Nicaragua. The agreement regulates regional migration for applicable categories, but does not automatically grant every foreign traveller the right to enter. Before travel, confirm exactly what authorisation a Russian citizen needs, how the permitted stay within the region is calculated and how entry at a land border is processed.

**Belize and Costa Rica do not belong to CA-4.** Costa Rica's current entry category, onward ticket, proof of funds, any vaccination documentation required by the route of arrival, and passport requirements all need to be checked separately. The complete eight-country tour also visits Mexico: the electronic SAE authorisation for Russian citizens applies to arrival **by air**, not as a universal permit for entry overland.

## Currencies and payments in the four countries

| Country | Local currency |
|---|---|
| Belize | Belize dollar (BZD) |
| Guatemala | Quetzal (GTQ) |
| Honduras | Lempira (HNL) |
| Costa Rica | Costa Rican colón (CRC) |

The Belize dollar is pegged to the US dollar at the official rate of **2 BZD to 1 USD**. That does not mean every tourism business is obliged to accept US-dollar cash or that exchange and change are always commission-free. In the other three countries, local currency is often more practical for spending at markets, cafés and in smaller towns.

For cards issued by Russian banks, overseas payment availability is especially important to verify before departure: a payment-system logo or a merchant's terminal does not guarantee that an individual card will work. We can help prepare a list of expected expenses and identify stops where an authorised cash reserve may be useful. The actual payment method and applicable restrictions must be discussed individually.

## Weather, altitude and clothes for different climates

Caracol and San Ignacio are generally hotter and more humid than Guatemala's highland stops. The programme includes an ascent of Pacaya from approximately **1,900 to 2,300 metres**, so a light jacket and comfortable shoes will be useful even after tropical heat. In Copán, carry water and sun protection for walks around the archaeological park.

Costa Rica adds several microclimates. Monteverde is cooler and mistier, Arenal can be humid, and the Caribbean side around Tortuguero does not experience the same clearly defined dry season as the Pacific side. A generic recommendation to 'travel in the dry season' is therefore insufficient for every stop. Compare the actual regions and months of the planned journey.

A practical packing list includes lightweight quick-drying clothes, a waterproof outer layer, closed shoes for rocky trails, sun protection and insect repellent. The day at El Tigre Waterfalls includes approximately **three hours of hiking**, with river crossings and rocks, followed by about 35 minutes on horseback. Discuss physical demands and any restrictions before booking.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is it possible to visit only Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Costa Rica?

A route like that can be discussed individually. The ready-made programme in this catalogue covers eight countries and 26 days. A four-country version would need separately confirmed domestic flights or overland transit through other countries.

### Can one visa be used for all four countries?

There is no universal basis for assuming a single visa covers all four. CA-4 includes Guatemala and Honduras, together with El Salvador and Nicaragua. Belize and Costa Rica have separate entry rules; nationality and passport type matter.

### Does the ready-made tour include Belize's beaches and reefs?

Belize is represented on this 26-day itinerary by San Ignacio, Caracol, Rio Frio Cave and the Rio On Pools. No barrier reef or island programme is specified. To visit Belize's marine areas, discuss a different or extended option.

### Is specialist trekking equipment needed?

The programme includes an ascent of Pacaya and a more demanding hiking section at El Tigre. Closed footwear with good grip and protection from rain and sun are needed; exact requirements and the possibility of a gentler pace should be agreed according to travellers' abilities.

The tour description confirms guided excursions in English. Russian-speaking assistance can be discussed separately, but should not be assumed to be included without confirmation.

## What adventures does the programme include?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The current [“Central America: Eight Countries in 26 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) travels through Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. The [four-country selection](/multi-country/belize_costa-rica_guatemala_honduras/) reflects their presence on that route. It does not mean there is a direct transfer from Honduras to Costa Rica without other stops.

The physical demands vary substantially. The clearest hiking activities are the ascent of Pacaya in Guatemala and the walk to El Tigre Waterfalls in Costa Rica. Caracol, Tikal and Copán are primarily archaeological attractions: walking through ancient cities is not the same as a sporting trek.

## Belize: Caracol, pine forests and Rio On

After arriving in Belize City, travellers transfer to [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/). The following day covers ancient Caracol, including an ascent of Caana, [Mountain Pine Ridge Reserve](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/), [Rio Frio Cave](/belize/place/rio-frio-cave/) and the [Rio On natural pools](/belize/place/rio-on-pools/). Swimming and relaxation at the pools are included in the schedule.

The day combines a historical excursion with stops in forests and along rivers. Comfortable shoes are helpful for climbing steps and walking over rocks. The itinerary does not, however, include technical caving, a dedicated white-water rafting activity or a multiday jungle trek. An overland crossing into Guatemala follows the Belizean section.

## Guatemala: Tikal, Pacaya and Lake Atitlán

At [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), travellers explore Maya temples amid tropical forest. The route then passes through [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/) towards [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/). A genuine hiking ascent is scheduled here: approximately **1,900 to 2,300 metres above sea level**. The upper point of the advertised walk is below the volcano's summit, so visiting the crater must not be promised.

After descending, the group travels to [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), explores local villages and takes a boat excursion. Guatemala thus combines walking activity, archaeology and local culture. The physical demands of Pacaya should be considered when choosing the route, and access to particular areas depends on current visitor conditions.

## Honduras: Copán and Maya heritage

From the Atitlán region, the tour heads into Honduras for a visit to [Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/). Guests explore the carved stelae and Hieroglyphic Stairway. This is a major centre of the ancient Maya civilisation, famous for inscriptions and architecture.

The Honduran day does not include a difficult mountain trek or rafting. It is a walking tour of an archaeological complex. After Copán, the itinerary continues through El Salvador and Nicaragua. Only then does the journey reach Costa Rica. This order needs to be considered even when the catalogue displays just four selected countries.

## Costa Rica: canopy, El Tigre and Arenal

A cloud forest walk and a canopy activity are planned in [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). The participation rules and those of the specific operator need to be clarified for the canopy experience: the tour description does not set universal eligibility limits for every traveller.

At [El Tigre Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/el-tigre-waterfalls/), the programme includes **approximately three hours of walking** along rocky trails and across rivers, at moderate to strenuous difficulty. A light snack and about 35 minutes on horseback follow. This day should be assessed in advance for physical fitness and comfort on wet ground.

Near [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), visitors explore hanging bridges and the Los Tucanes trail among old lava flows. Later, they take boat excursions on the canals of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). The nature itinerary becomes less physically demanding here, although sightings of particular animals remain a matter of chance.
